description: Sequencer that plays a plain-text table: one row per step, one column per output, written in the maker's RhythML notation

params.text: Switches the Index input between reading a phasor across the whole sequence and reading a row number as a voltage

inputs.text: A rising edge above 1V moves on one row, wrapping round at the end of the sequence
A rising edge above 1V returns to the first row, and the step inputs are ignored for the next 5ms
Sets the current row directly, the first row at 0V and the last at 10V, or by row number counted from zero when the switch is set to absolute; a cable here stops both step inputs from working
A rising edge above 1V moves back one row, wrapping round at the start of the sequence
The voltages written into the text of the current row when Record Trigger fires, one channel per column
A rising edge above 1V writes the Record In voltages into the current row; a mono cable writes every Record In channel at once, while each channel of a polyphonic cable writes only its own column

outputs.text: Every column of the current row on one cable, with the channel count set by the polyphony mode on the menu
The voltage the current row gives that column: the cell's own value, 10V for a gate, a 1ms pulse for a trigger, or the value held over from an earlier row when the cell is blank
The position in the sequence, 0V on the first row rising to 10V on the last
The number of the current row as a voltage, 1V on the first row and rising a volt per row

notes: the module plays nothing until you click the black panel and type a sequence: one row per line, cells separated by commas, one column per output jack.
click outside the text to commit an edit and parse it, or press Ctrl and Enter to commit without leaving the text.
Ctrl and the bracket keys change the text size, and while the module is playing the text scrolls to keep the current row centred.
drag the right-hand edge of the panel to make the module wider or narrower.
a cell takes a decimal voltage, a percentage where 100% is 10V, a note name such as C4 or G#3, a MIDI number as m60, semitones as s7, cents as 100ct, or a frequency as 261.63Hz; C4 is 0V.
in a cell, W or the bar character holds 10V for the whole step, T or the caret gives 0V for 1ms then 10V for 1ms then 0V, and X or the underscore drops to 0V for 1ms and then holds 10V.
a cell the parser cannot read gives 0V, and anything after a question mark in a cell is a comment.
comments in the first row are taken as column labels and become the names Rack shows when you hover the output jacks.
a Page expander placed immediately to the right carries columns 17 onwards, and further Pages after it carry sixteen more each.
menu: Widest row (constant channels) — the polyphonic output always carries as many channels as the widest row of the sequence
Non-blank cells only (variable) — the polyphonic output carries only the filled cells of the current row, packed into consecutive channels
Up to last non-blank (per row) — the polyphonic output carries the current row through to its last filled cell, blanks in the middle keeping their place; a new module starts here
Decimal (4 decimal places) — recorded voltages are written into the text as decimals such as 0.5833
Note names (quantized to semitones) — recorded voltages are rounded to the nearest semitone and written into the text as note names such as C4 or G#5

inputs.0: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.1: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.3: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
